pr_title: Add support for encrypting files fetched to local
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY
Added support to encrypt files fetched to local into vaults. Fixes #79802.

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Feature Pull Request

##### COMPONENT NAME
ansible.builtin.fetch

##### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
Added two new parameters to ansible.builtin.fetch:
encrypt: boolean
vault_id: string
If encryption is enabled, then locally stored file is encrypted into given vault.

Well, the final decision whether including this makes sense or not is up to you, the ansible team. But it would be good to resolve this before I spend more time polishing the patch :-). It would definitely make ansible more useful for me. Right now, we are using gpg encrypted files (gpg called via shell on the target) to encrypt files such as private backup keys. But gpg is not idempotent due to random salt, so it's a pain to work with.

I don't think copy, lineinfile, blockinfile etc. need any support for encryption. I don't see any use for vault encrypted files on the target, vaults are IMHO, meant solely for storing private data in the (public) ansible playbook repository. So the modules you mention can have support for decryption (copy already has, others does not seem to), but that's completely unrelated to this change.

Coming back after a while, I still want to know what is the general feeling about this proposed change in the ansible team. Shall I continue polishing the patch in the hopes to get it eventually merged one day? Or should I abandon all my hopes and spend my time on something more productive? :-)
We decided internally to go with https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/79864#pullrequestreview-1287877737 option. Thanks for the contribution.

issue_context.title: Extended Vault support: encrypting files copied from the target
issue_context.body:
### Summary

The #7298 extended the copy module to allow decrypting vaulted files being copied to the target. I would like to propose now to extend also the ansible.builtin.fetch module with the ability to encrypt files being copied from the target.
One of my use cases is: I generate a new lxc container, install ssh server. That generates private ssh machine key. On clients trying to connect, this key must be accepted (that's done manually for now). When I want to re-generate the lxc container later, I don't want to go to all clients and re-approve the ssh server key, so I am restoring the private ssh key.
Right now, my playbook copies the key to local machine and prints a message instructing to use ansible-vault to encrypt the file manually before commiting it to git repo, but I would like to avoid this manual step.
FWIW, I also looked at vault filter, but according to #79298, this seems it is not going to work.

### Issue Type

Feature Idea

### Component Name

ansible.builtin.fetch module

### Additional Information

As you can't do autodetection of vault files when encrypting, new parameters of the fetch module would have to be added. I suppose that one boolean parameter to enable encryption and one optional string with vault_id should be sufficient.
Would there be interest in such a feature? I may look into creating a patch, if it looks like something acceptable.

### Code of Conduct

- [X] I agree to follow the Ansible Code of Conduct

I'm confused by the indication that the copy module needs modification.  I'm assuming you mean the fetch module since you are fetching a file from a target to the local machine.  This could be done, but there will be complexities about choosing the vault ID to encrypt with.

The core team has no intention of implementing this, but we would entertain a change to the `fetch` action plugin to encrypt the local file that has been fetched.  Implementing idempotency would become rather complex here as well.

Thanks for the quick reaction. You are of course correct, I meant ansible.builtin.fetch. Sorry for the confusion.
As I wrote, vault_id would have to be one of the parameters, in case you are using more than one. If not provided, either the first one gets used, or an error is raised. I don't think any usable autodetection would be possible in a generic case.
Regarding idempotency, I think it is solvable, but I admit I haven't looked at the code yet. So far, I looked at the copy module to see how the decryption was done (hence the confusion :-) ).
So I take it the are no direct objections to this idea, so I will try my luck at putting something together :-).

Two notes:
- I tried to limit the number of changed files, basically putting all changes into the fetch.py module itself. This however means I am accessing some stuff which may be considered as "private", as e.g. the vault instance in data loader. If this is a problem, I can change the architecture to add supporting functions to data loader/vault and separate these, jut let me know what is the preferred way.
- If the encryption is enabled, the vault_id parameter is mandatory. That means there is no support for unnamed vaults. Again, if this is a problem, let me know. However changing this would raise some questions, e.g. which vault to pick if we have available more than one :-).

review_comments:
not sure we need 2 values here, I would add `vault:` parameter, it should either match a vault id OR be the vault secret itself. 

When not specified, no encryption is used.

One downside of this is that if the user makes a typo in vault id, then there is no error, the file is silently encrypted with that string as a secret, and the "secret" is then plainly visible in the playbook. Possibly insecure behavior. What about two params, vault_id and secret, and if any of the two is defined, encryption is enabled? (Does it make sense to have both defined? Can we specify secret and vault_id independently? Won't be there problems with decryption then?)

This can cause an error by attempting to encrypt data that's already been encrypted with the same vault_id. To reproduce, I'm using this task:
```
  - name: Storing a file in an encrypted vault
    ansible.builtin.fetch:
      src: /tmp/encrypted
      dest: /tmp/dest
      flat: yes
      encrypt: yes
```
and `/tmp/encrypted` is encrypted with the default vault_id, and /tmp/dest exists and contains plaintext. I would expect the dest to be overwritten, but not for the source to be re-encrypted with the same vault_id, but I get:

```
fatal: [localhost]: FAILED! => {
    "msg": "input is already encrypted"
}
```

Well, never thought that someone would store vault encrypted file on the target, and then try to fetch it with encryption enabled... What would be the use case for storing encrypted file on the target? How can you put it there, copy module would automatically decrypt on the fly? (or can it be forced not to decrypt? Haven't checked.).
OK, I will check if it's possible to prevent double encryption...

Hmm, thinking about it more, I don't know if we really want to go this path. Assuming the remote file can be already encrypted, it adds quite a lot of possible combinations to the mix.
What if the remote is encrypted and we have encrypt=false? Should we decrypt the file? Not backwards compatible.
What if the remote is encrypted with different vault_id, should we re-encrypt it? What if we don't have credentials to decrypt the original, should we fail?
My suggestion is to ignore this corner case. If someone wants to copy already encrypted file, encrypt=false will work as it is working now, without re-encryption.
Suggestions?

You're probably right that the error is fine from a user-perspective. When I traced the code, I was interested in the codepath that inspects whether the source is encrypted and determines re_encrypt_needed, because I wasn't sure why the source would be encrypted. So I created a contrived example using an encrypted source to get to that codepath and see what happens if it theoretically shouldn't  need to be re-encrypted.

It sounds like this wasn't what you intended though - I think the logic for re_encrypt_needed can be removed in that case. This diff seems to pass with your tests:

```diff
diff --git a/lib/ansible/plugins/action/fetch.py b/lib/ansible/plugins/action/fetch.py
index af7de7be7a..73f1b33b8e 100644
--- a/lib/ansible/plugins/action/fetch.py
+++ b/lib/ansible/plugins/action/fetch.py
@@ -182,15 +182,15 @@ class ActionModule(ActionBase):
                             raise AnsibleParserError("A vault password or secret must be specified to decrypt %s" % to_native(dest))
 
                         data, vault_id_used, vault_secret_used = self._loader._vault.decrypt_and_get_vault_id(data, filename=dest)
-                        local_encrypted = True
-                        local_checksum = checksum_s(data)
-                        re_encrypt_needed = (vault_id_used != vault_id or vault_secret_used != vault_secret)
+                        if vault_id_used == vault_id or vault_secret_used == vault_secret:
+                            local_encrypted = True
+                            local_checksum = checksum_s(data)
 
             # calculate checksum for the local file
             if not local_encrypted:
                 local_checksum = checksum(dest)
 
-            if remote_checksum != local_checksum or local_encrypted != encrypt or re_encrypt_needed:
+            if remote_checksum != local_checksum:
                 # create the containing directories, if needed
                 makedirs_safe(os.path.dirname(dest))
```

That diff would also resolve https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/79864#discussion_r1098748255, since we'd no long decrypt random encrypted files with encrypt omitted.

You were right, my logic in this area was flawed. I made a change, please check if it is better now.
If you fetch encrypted file and specify encrypt=true, the file will still be double encrypted (user error I would say), but if you specify encrypt=no, then the file is transferred as is, not conversion done.
I'm not sure what the implications of `support: full` are- @bcoca?
It's mostly just documentation, there's no strict standard AFAIK.
Stolen from copy module :-), feel free to change to whatever suits better.

```    
vault:
      description: Can automatically decrypt Ansible vaulted files
```
in this case it is 'encrypt'
Where is this description coming from? What do you suggest to put to the description instead of full then, "can encrypt into vaulted files" ?
now i'm thinking we need `vault:` with choices `decrypt/encrypt/full`

and for fetch ... what about a feature that decrypts automatically the fetched content if it is a vault? this is what we normally do in other actions. this is the first time we are looking at encrypting from the action itself (i tried to avoid this by adding the `vault` filrer).
OK, I will put there "encrypt" and see what happens :-).

Does not pass sanity test without updating the attribute definitions. Should I update these as well? A bit out of scope for this ticket, though.
On the other hand, not sure how important this is, IMHO decryption in fetch does not make sense (as encryption in copy module, also not implemented AFAIK), so specifying full here is probably good as well.
